text:
Kara: heads up — p99 for /v2/generate looks off in the dashboard (p99 ~420ms) but raw traces cluster ~120ms. noticed after the aliasing change. @Mike @Sanjay
Mike: hmm, did we lose any routing tags in the rollup keys? :thinking:
Sanjay: quick check — the console rollup query is `group_by(endpoint_name)` only. we rolled out route aliasing last week so route=canary vs route=stable might be collapsing.
Kara: here’s the exact console query we run: ```SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 99) FROM metric_rollups WHERE endpoint = '/v2/generate' AND window='5m'``` — but our traces have tags `route=canary`, `variant=quantized` so they should be separate.
Mike: right — proxy strips route tags before emitting metrics for cost/cardinality reasons. that would fold canary+stable into one rollup and inflate tail.
Alyssa: could also be sampling bias: canary traffic is sparse but high-latency. when merged it skews the p99.
DevBot: Deploy 4523 of eng-runtime succeeded to prod (route-aliasing) at 2415006900
Sanjay: short-term fix idea: conditionally include `route_alias` in rollup_key only when `sample_count > 500` in the window. pseudocode: ```if sample_count(window) > 500: rollup_key += route_alias```
Kara: that avoids runaway cardinality for low-traffic endpoints. but need to be careful with rollup merge semantics — t-digest merges are order-insensitive but dropping tags changes the grouping.
Mike: agree. alternative: keep rollups unchanged but add a derived metric `p99_by_route` computed offline for routes with >500 samples, then surface in console as an expansion.
Alyssa: UX-wise, we'd want a small badge: "Split by route (approx)" and a hover explaining the threshold. avoids surprising product teams.
Sanjay: I pushed a tiny patch to add the conditional key: ```diff --git a/rollup/service.py b/rollup/service.py
@@ -128,6 +128,12 @@ def key_for(sample):
    key = (endpoint_name, team_id)
+    if sample_count_recent(endpoint_name) > 500:
+        key = key + (sample.route_alias,)
    return key
```
Kara: can we add a metric to monitor cardinality delta after this deploy? want an auto rollback if unique_keys_rate spikes > 10%.
Mike: yes, add `unique_rollup_keys_rate` alert with 15m lookback. I can add to the canary playbook.
Alyssa: also add console note: "Percentiles may be aggregated across routes when traffic is low" so dashboards don't get misinterpreted.
Kara: sounds good — I'll kick off a small canary, monitor `p99_raw_vs_rollup` and `unique_rollup_keys_rate`. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Mike: filing a follow-up doc and linking datapoints: https://intranet.internal/notes/perc-labeling-routing-gap-2415
Alyssa: adding a short blurb in the rollout checklist.
Kara: will update ops oncall if we see >5% deviation in p99 within 30m after patch.
